prompt: A photo app is 92% accurate overall but much worse on night photos. Explain how this can happen, and what would actually fix it.

criteria.label: Explains the average hiding a gap
criteria.look_for: a small group's failures barely move the overall number

criteria.label: Names the data cause
criteria.look_for: night photos were rare in the training data

criteria.label: Gives a fix that works
criteria.look_for: add or cover the missing group (night photos) and report accuracy for each group; more of the same data does not help

reference: The 92% is an average across everyone tested. Night photos were rare in the training data, so the model learned them poorly, and because they are a small part of the test set, their errors barely move the average. Adding more daytime photos would not help; adding night photos to training and reporting accuracy separately for day and night would.
